utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, the programme which I suggest for this morning is that we hear the witness until a few minutes after eleven. We will then take the break, and it may be a bit shorter than usual, and then about half past we will hear the Defence ex parte submissions. We have to finish at twenty to one. An hour is said to be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So there is unlikely to be evidence beyond the midmorning break or there won't be.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In relation to the next witness: First of all, there was a failure to disclose a Bosnia and Herzegovina statement upon which there is effectively no or almost no reliance in the summary. It's been disclosed now last night. Just so I can explain how this has happened -- it's happened once before -- the searching of material is obviously a big exercise and is not a physical exercise, it's an electronic one to a degree. It's been done at the earlier stage of disclosure. From time to time it's been repeated in respect of particular witnesses, but, of course, once witnesses come here a further and entirely fresh process of expiration or material is undertaken and it's at that stage that this particular statement was revealed. As I say, it hasn't been relied upon but it has now been served and it's of only a little under two sides, and I an apologise, of course, for any inconvenience caused. In respect of this witness, we seek protection. The Court will see that the protection sought is the type of which it is least fond; namely, a closed session. That's not because, in one sense, the man requires a fully closed session, it's because -- if we're in open session, I suppose I ought now to ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 10.59 a.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 6th day of December, 1999, at 9.30 a.m.
